newsitem.title: USA: US late cash gasoline down one cent, heat recovers.
newsitem.headline: US late cash gasoline down one cent, heat recovers.

text.p: U.S. cash gasoline fell a full cent in late trade Monday but heating oil reclaimed most of its sharp intraday losses tracking a rebound Monday in NYMEX futures, players said.
Dealings were described as very thin, however, as many players took the day off for Yom Kippur, the holy Jewish holiday.
Gasoline differentials firmed slightly in the Gulf Coast, players said, as refineries continued to shift their focus to maximal production of distillates ahead of winter.
Gulf Coast 28th-cycle conventional unleaded M3 grade gasoline was offered at 3.75 cents under October futures, with reformulated A3 grade offered at 2.10 cents under.

"The switch from gasoline to heating oil is tightening gasoline supplies a bit," one Gulf trader said, adding refineries were more motivated than usual to focus on heat because of its current seasonally high prices and low domestic stocks.

Differentials held steady on New York Harbor M4-grade conventional gasoline, meanwhile, with offers at 1.25 cents below the print, traders said. Reformulated A2-grade fuel was offered at even with the print, a touch firmer than Friday.
